naming_rule: <amine>-<BL>-<thiol>, e.g. T3A-L5-C10 = amine core T3A + bispecific linker L5 + 1-decanethiol. The amine tokens (70, 75, 80, 110, 113, 114, 400) are conventional lipidoid amine catalogue numbers and encode nothing about structure; T3A is this paper's own token for tris(3-aminopropyl)amine. L1-L8 are linker identities, not lengths, and the series is not a length ladder (L1 cyclohexyl, L2 pyridyldithio, L3/L4/L5 = 1/3/5 CH2, L6/L7/L8 = PEG1/2/3). Cn is the literal carbon count of a linear 1-alkanethiol.
degree_of_substitution: One BL+thiol arm per primary amine: 1 for 70/75/80/400, 2 for 113/114, 3 for 110/T3A. Set by the amine:BL:thiol feed ratios in Table S1 (1:1.05:1.1, 1:2.05:2.1, 1:3.05:3.1) and confirmed by product mass balance for 70, 110, 113, 400 and T3A; not evidenced for 114 or 80.
reaction_description: One-pot three-component reaction (BL-3CR). The amine is acylated by the NHS ester to an amide and the alkyl-thiol adds to the maleimide to give a thiosuccinimide. Amines and alkyl-thiols dissolved in ethanol, BLs in DMF; all three combined in a 2 mL glass vial and reacted at 80 C with magnetic stirring (800 rpm) for 4 h, catalyst-free; blow-dried under N2 to remove ethanol and unreacted volatile amines and thiols; crude dissolved in ethanol (5 mg/mL) and stored at 4 C for in vitro screening. For in vivo work lipids were purified by flash chromatography (silica, DCM/methanol 3/1) to >95% purity. Exception: with L2 (SPDP) the second step is thiol-disulfide exchange releasing 2-pyridinethione, giving a disulfide rather than a thiosuccinimide.
ambiguity_note: Library 1, 320 lipids (8 amines x 8 BLs x 5 thiols). Cells seeded at 1e4 per well in 96-well transparent black plates. Crude unpurified lipids were used for this screen. The Methods cite 'Tables S1, S3' for the feed molar ratios, but the ratios are in Tables S1 and S2 (S3 is the protein-corona table). The 20:1 ratio is written 'lipid/mRNA' in the Results and 'LNP/mRNA' in the Methods and is never defined as ionizable-lipid-to-mRNA - see CHK17.
